articles.title: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Figma and its CEO are being sued by a current employee for alleged sexual harassment and discrimination.
articles.body_text: A Figma engineer is suing the design software company and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct. The lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the company’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse. “Figma was my dream company for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.” Park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially. When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma said, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.” Park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the company would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.” Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit. Park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit. Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior. The lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It says the company’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved. In March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching plan, which she completed in late 2023. Changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.
articles.body_text: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself. “Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.” Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge. The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available , and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed. Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language. Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process. Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision. Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta. articles.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.
articles.body_text: AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents. Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman , who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator. Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April. “We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day. The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading launches like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others. The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a new level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models. Currently, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable. Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do. Supertake’s users’ ideas are tracked on a leaderboard on the site, so others who agree can invest alongside them. For instance, there’s currently an idea on the leaderboard about looksmaxxing and longevity becoming more of a trend, where the portfolio includes certain pharma and cosmetic companies that could potentially benefit. For now, these portfolios consist of stock picks, but the team wants to expand the service over time to handle other types of transactions, like shorts, derivatives, perpetuals, long exposure, or even prediction markets — the latter handled through partnerships with companies in that space. Despite these “takes” seeming like bets on what could happen next in a given market, Murr stresses that this doesn’t make Supertake itself a prediction market. “We think it’s a novel and very much improved way to create what was previously considered the robo-advisor experience,” he says. “When that came out, it had this amazing vision and direction of allowing people to have digital asset management. We think now is actually the time for that, with AI agents being so widely proliferated.”

articles.title: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "The mistake has been corrected," Elon Musk chimed in.
articles.body_text: A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning. “The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return. The mistake has been corrected https://t.co/UKvEng9rCD Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.” Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang. “Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji. Glad to see @JensenHuang back. 👏 https://t.co/WrUjvmEyVi Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who had been among 200,000 signatories on an open letter calling for Huang’s reinstatement, wrote on X, “Jensen’s return will be a demonstration of American resiliency to corporate, political and journalistic missteps.” Another signatory on the open letter, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, who had similarly been driven out of the company he founded after scandals , also voiced his support for Huang on X.

articles.title: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government.
articles.body_text: Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday. The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.” Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.” Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China . The company has denied wrongdoing. TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds. After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang. articles.body_text: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online. The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump. After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd. “Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.” Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. articles.title: Amazon snaps up Decart's AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s AI optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal.
articles.body_text: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart. The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg. Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware. As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post . “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.” Amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far. articles.title: Meta throws out its net-zero goal — its competitors should be furious | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta walked back its 2030 net-zero goal in its 2026 sustainability report, a decision that could send ripples throughout the tech industry.
articles.body_text: Meta’s new sustainability report buries the lead: The company is almost certain to miss its own goal to reach net zero by 2030, and it’s refusing to commit to a new timeline. “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the company’s 2026 sustainability report. That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout. Such is the risk of voluntary targets. Companies can make and break them with little to lose, betting — often rightly — that they can ignore them with just a small hit to public opinion, which is fickle anyway. (Remember the Cambridge Analytica scandal? Most people don’t.) There’s almost no risk to the bottom line. “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline and interim milestone. We’ll continue investing in emissions reductions and reporting our progress annually,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch. A few years ago, Meta was arguably one of the better corporate stewards of the climate. The company has been one of the largest purchasers of clean power, and it set ambitious goals for water conservation. More recently, though, its multibillion-dollar bet on natural gas at its Hyperion data center in Louisiana has undone much of that progress. Natural gas may burn cleaner and more efficiently than coal, but its impact on global warming can be just as bad when the leaky infrastructure needed to burn it is factored in. Despite years of clean power procurement, Meta’s greenhouse gas emissions have more than doubled in the last four years. Between 2024 and 2025, its data center emissions increased more than 12 times, and Hyperion isn’t online yet. That commitment to natural gas led to the company’s departure from RE100 , a corporate renewable energy initiative, in July. The company had been part of the group for a decade, though the two split after RE100 started requiring more rigorous reporting toward renewable energy targets. “When we set our net zero emissions goal, we anticipated steady growth, falling clean energy costs, and changes in the broader system that would enable progress at the pace we envisioned,” they added. “The reality has been far more complex. Demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected, arriving on a timeline measured in quarters rather than decades, and meeting it has meant building at a pace and scale the industry has never attempted.” That’s all true, but when put that way, it sounds like Meta has little agency in the matter. But the company’s decision to chase AI was a conscious one. You could argue that Meta has a fiduciary duty to chase after its peers, which have also dived headfirst into AI. But there’s precious little data to support the idea that AI will be a profit driver for a company like Meta, which is almost entirely consumer-focused.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The cybersecurity giant said that the deal to buy Zscaler, which provides zero-trust products to large enterprises, will better equip their customers to use AI agents.
articles.body_text: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the companies announced Monday. CrowdStrike and Zscaler said that the deal will create the “largest single addressable market” for cybersecurity, which will enable the companies to better position themselves for the AI era. Zscaler is a San Jose, California-based tech company that provides cloud cybersecurity products to about 8,000 enterprise companies. The company offers zero-trust technology, a security feature that requires employees to authenticate each and every time they access an internal system or resource. The aim is to protect against hackers from stealing credentials and using them to gain unfettered access to a company’s network. CrowdStrike, which secures the computers, laptops, phones, and other devices connected to a company’s network, said the deal will unite its endpoint protection software with Zscaler’s zero-trust platform to better defend their customers against data breaches. By combining the two products, CrowdStrike and Zscaler say that they can offer “superior protection” to their customers. In remarks on Monday, the companies said that the acquisition will help customers safely adopt AI. The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close around this time next year. articles.title: Uber will now let drivers and riders record audio during trips for safety
articles.summary: Uber announced its new safety features for both rider and driver safety set to be released later this month and early 2022. The new features include audio recording, audible seat belt alerts, and enhanced RideCheck features.
articles.body_text: Uber is releasing its audio-recording feature to three US cities later this month, Uber said in its press release. At the beginning of a trip, riders and drivers can enable this feature by clicking the shield icon in the app’s Safety Toolkit and selecting “Record Audio.” While both riders and drivers can record individual trips, drivers have the option to leave the feature on while they’re actively seeking rides. The app will notify the rider if the driver is using the feature. Uber first launched audio recording in Latin America in 2019. The move is the first in-app feature that provides audio documentation of rides. Uber allows drivers to use their own dashcams to record rides on their own if local laws permit it. As for audio file privacy, the file is encrypted and stored on rider and driver’s devices, but no one can listen to the audio, even Uber. If either the rider or driver decides to submit a safety report, they can attach the audio file, and a trained Uber safety agent will decrypt and review the recording. Along with audio recording, Uber is releasing audible seat belt alerts soon, according to the press release. The seat belt alert will come from the driver’s phone, and the rider will receive a push notification reminding them to put on their seat belt. Uber said that this feature will be available in the US in early 2022. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration — or NHTSA — reported that in 2020, the national seat belt use rate was 90.3 percent. NHTSA also reported that of the 22,415 passenger vehicle occupants killed in 2019, 47 percent were not wearing seat belts. NHTSA said they found no significant changes in seat belt use from 2019 to 2020. Uber also announced enhancements for its RideCheck feature, first launched in 2019 to detect accidents and unusual long stops. Now, RideCheck can now detect when Uber drivers take an unexpected route or when a trip ends abruptly before the final destination. If detected, riders and drivers will receive a notification to make sure everything is safe. Uber first published a safety report in 2019 looking at data between 2017 and 2018 following increased complaints from occupants regarding its safety practices. Ultimately, these observations included the safety of drivers who have also complained to the company about rider behavior. Uber has been steadily releasing new safety features in response to both riders and drivers experiencing unsafe conditions during their trips, including allegations of sexual assault. In March, Uber, along with its competitor Lyft, announced that it would share information about drivers who were deactivated for committing serious offenses.

Steven Spielberg’s Ready Player One improves immensely on the book
articles.summary: Ernest Cline’s fast-moving, bestselling novel was a treasure trove for pop-culture junkies. But the endless references to video games and movies work better on the screen, where most of them originated in the first place.
articles.body_text: Fans tend to either love or hate Ernest Cline’s bestselling 2011 novel Ready Player One. There are legitimate reasons for both reactions. On the love side: it’s a light, airy pop confection, crammed with familiar cultural references, which Cline recontextualizes in surprising ways. On the hate side: the prose can be extremely clumsy, as it is in this paragraph where teenage protagonist Wade Watts describes the virtual car he constructed for himself in the vast online world where he spends most of his waking hours: > The DeLorean came outfitted with a (nonfunctioning) flux capacitor, but I’d made several additions to its equipment and appearance. First, I’d installed an artificially intelligent onboard computer named KITT (purchased in an online auction) into the dashboard, along with a matching red Knight Rider scanner just above the DeLorean’s grill. Then I’d outfitted the car with an oscillation overthruster, a device that allowed it to travel through solid matter. Finally, to complete my ‘80s super-vehicle theme, I’d slapped a Ghostbusters logo on each of the DeLorean’s gull-wing doors, then added personalized plates that read ECTO-88. That’s a lot of awkward verbiage to say two pretty basic things: people in virtual reality can express their personal tastes through their avatars in hyper-specific ways, and Cline is so obsessed with the culture of the 1980s — the geek-fodder of his youth — that he thinks it’s compelling even in the form of a shopping list. The book is a fast-paced adventure, but this kind of unwieldy lump of mix-and-match nostalgia acts as a roadblock. There’s no attempt to consider why Wade finds these specific objects appealing, out of the billion options available to him. The book assumes up front that readers find everything in this list as unbearably cool as Cline does, and that just running down an exhaustive list of Wade’s favorite things is enough to make him appealing, relatable, and enviable. Steven Spielberg’s new film adaptation of Ready Player One prominently features that same car, but in a context that improves it immensely. Spielberg doesn’t have Wade talk audiences through it, and he doesn’t spell out the references. He just slaps the car down in the middle of a tremendous early action scene, where it’s prominent, distinctive, and memorable. Fans who want the full nostalgia trip, who want to wring every Easter egg out of the experience, will eventually be able to pause the movie and frame-by-frame through it, looking for the flux capacitor on the dashboard, checking the plates, and scanning for extra bonus material. But in the middle of the action, even to people who’ve never seen the Back to the Future movies and aren’t vibing on the connection, the car doesn’t need explaining. It’s just a sleek piece of visual energy, one breathless element among dozens of others. It’s not a citation or a list. It’s an effortless, integrated piece of the action. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cSp1dM2Vj48] That dynamic stretches throughout Ready Player One, scripted by Cline and X-Men: The Last Stand writer Zak Penn, and directed by Spielberg as a whiplash-fast tear through a world-spanning, all-encompassing video game. The story, which mostly takes place in the virtual-reality world called The OASIS, rarely slows down enough to explain the references, or geek out over them the way the book does. It’s still a visual festival of ‘80s culture that sometimes hinges significant jokes on the assumption that the audience knows the filmography of Robert Zemeckis, or will chortle over a reference to Monty Python and the Holy Grail. But the film improves significantly on the book by prioritizing the story over the signifiers. The hardcore pop-culture crowd that is this movie’s ultimate intended audience will have plenty to pore over and pick apart in this film. But the story moves briskly enough, and with enough giant-sized, screen-friendly excitement, that it doesn’t feel like it’s aimed solely and specifically at them. Some of that speed comes at the expense of artistry. Ready Player One opens by laboriously climbing a mountain of voiceover, explaining the setting: the year is 2045, and the world is terrible. Most people live in depressing poverty, and spend as much time as possible jacked into the fantasy world of the OASIS. There, they can be and do anything they want, or at least anything they can afford to buy with coins won in the universe’s eternally running video game arenas. The OASIS was created by reclusive genius James Halliday (Bridge of Spies’ Mark Rylance), who packed it with his own favorite culture. When he died, he created a three-part quest within the world, linked to his favorite films and games, but also tied to his own past regrets and frustrations. Whoever finds the three keys he’s hidden within the game world, and the ultimate Easter egg they unlock, will get full control of OASIS and Halliday’s vast fortune. The quest has created a subclass of “egg-hunters,” or “Gunters” — quest-obsessives whose full-time occupation is hunting down the keys. It’s also created an evil dystopian megacorp, run by former Halliday intern Nolan Sorrento (Ben Mendelsohn, of Rogue One and Starred Up), and devoted to gaining control of the OASIS to commercialize it. Wade (X-Men: Apocalypse’s Tye Sheridan) and his fellow Gunters — particularly too-cool-for-school solo hunter Art3mis (Olivia Cooke, also currently starring in the chilling Thoroughbreds) and Wade’s big mechanical buddy Aech (Master of None’s Lena Waithe) — all want the keys and the egg for their own personal reasons, though those are barely articulated. Cline’s book assumes everyone will know a DeLorean is cool; Spielberg’s film assumes the same thing about a teenage protagonist who loves playing video games. Wade (or Parzival, as he’s known in the OASIS) eventually develops an ethos, but for the most part, he’s like every other video gamer who’s ever sat down on a couch and hit “start” on the controller. He may appreciate the gameplay or the storyline or the people he meets online, but ultimately, he just wants that elusive win. He’s more a customized audience avatar than a real character, but that’s fitting for a world that’s so spottily drawn, at least outside of the virtual paradise where people prefer to spent their time. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/9820163/29ed3d416cd513893ea80d1e6c9a560e.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] The film version of Ready Player One has some major advantages over the book. The exposition is just as bald, but once it’s done, Spielberg can focus on the endless dynamism of a world where anything is possible. As Wade and others follow their quest through races, battles, and puzzles, they encounter a dizzying blur of visual references that act as “Hey, remember this?” in-jokes with the audience, including some major ones that weren’t in the book. But the filmmakers also delve into Halliday’s past and his wounded psyche, in a way that gradually becomes a little touching and tragic. (A conversation with Halliday’s online avatar closely recalls a similar scene with Professor Falken in WarGames, and carries the same sense of melancholy.) The film also goes further than the book in laying out why Halliday’s retreat into a fantasy world wasn’t necessarily good for anyone — especially not for Halliday himself. No matter how validating the onscreen gags are, they’re still a reminder of a man who found more emotional resonance in Jurassic Park’s T-Rex than in a connection with a living human being. The film inevitably has its cake and eats it too when it comes to addressing wish-fulfillment fantasy and delirious nostalgia: the story can only push so far in sorrowing over Halliday’s surrender and retreat from the world, while still turning every rambunctious game setpiece into a celebration of Cline’s favorite culture. Ready Player One is so heavily inspired by and inflected with the broad, black-and-white morality of ‘80s geek culture that any attempt to find the gray areas feels slightly daring, even as it feels slightly out of place. Given that Sorrento is a buttoned-down, stony-faced idea-thief of an evil overlord, straight out of Tron, there’s not a lot of room for narrative nuance in this story. But at least Cline and Penn make the effort, acknowledging some of the biggest complaints leveled at Cline’s book, and trying to take the story a little deeper. The film version does carry over some of the book’s most notable flaws, especially a suspicious reliance on narrative convenience and coincidence. The characters are thinly drawn, and most of them are little more than cool avatars and signature moves. There’s no sense that anyone involved with the story really cares about the details of the real world in this crapsack future, given how little the real-world scenes hold together. And the film takes a particularly feather-light approach to what should be significant emotions, especially when a death that should devastate Wade is shrugged off within seconds, then brought back out for a cheap, unearned moment much later. Spielberg’s signature sentiment is operating in full force, as he builds up one highly symbolic confrontation solely for the feelings of triumph and justice it creates, and then has it come to exactly nothing. And in places, the story jumps forward so quickly that it feels like necessary connective scenes are simply missing. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/10408527/ready_player_one.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] Unequivocally, the film’s biggest problem is the half-assed love story between Wade and Art3mis, which operates on approximately 75 percent wish-fulfillment and 25 percent apathetic inevitability. When they first encounter each other, Wade is starstruck: he knows Art3mis from her online cool-girl rep, and watching her in action, he sees her as an über-badass with leet skillz and an appealingly punk devil-may-care attitude. It’s a short, shocking jump from there to him telling her he loves her. What follows should be important and telling — she reminds him that they don’t know each other, that he’s seeing an online avatar and a mental picture he’s largely invented. (And, of course, he thinks they’re perfect for each other because she gets his references.) But the film never follows through on that mature and useful point. The insta-relationship that develops between them is as inauthentic and insulting as the central romance in Edgar Wright’s Scott Pilgrim Vs. The World, without any of the sense of irony or intentionality. It’s bad enough to follow the “hero wins the girl as a prize” model without examining it at all. It’s worse still to have the characters examine it, find the flaws, then instantly forget about them. This isn’t a movie with a long memory (except when it’s reaching back 40 years for visual gags), but it’s infuriating to see it try to examine its own tropes responsibly, then take no steps whatsoever to address the issues it raises. And yet, when Wade is in his kitted-out DeLorean, tearing along a preposterously difficult game racetrack, menaced by King Kong and dodging flying debris as his fellow racers crash and burn, very little of that matters. The sheer dynamism and energy of the movie are compelling, even when the character drama isn’t. The action scenes are deliberately overclocked and overwhelming, turning Wade’s quest into a thrilling blur of fast-paced decisions and the endorphin-rush highs of a good gaming experience. More importantly, the film is overtly funny in ways that constantly remind the audience that there are people behind the game avatars, and specifically people who are sometimes young, self-absorbed, immature, and caught up in their own created self-images of badassery. The human frailties behind the game avatars is a reliable well of humor for Ready Player One, and the script takes full, hilarious advantage. And while the film’s real world gets left behind in the rush, the attention to detail during the OASIS scenes is absolutely astounding — not just the details Cline salivated over on the page, like that Knight Rider scanner in the grill of Wade’s car, but the subtle nuances, like the way Wade’s avatar constantly seems to be standing in a flattering breeze that ruffles his hair in the most winsome way possible, or the way Art3mis’ too-big anime eyes catch the light. The uncanny-valley effect is strong in these game avatars, but Spielberg uses it to his advantage, reminding his audience at every moment that what they’re seeing is mostly a fantasy, created by people who see image as almost everything. It’s a slick, sleek, surface fantasy, for sure. But for people who share Cline’s worldview, or identify with gamer culture in general, it’s an immense hit of validation and acknowledgement, delivered with joyful abandon and unmissable enthusiasm. All those feelings of love and obsession came through clearly on the page. But on the screen, they’re bigger and better, because they’re so much more intense, and so much closer to the memorable images that turned Cline into an obsessive in the first place. This review was initially published after Ready Player One’s premiere at the 2018 SXSW festival in Austin, Texas. The film arrives in theaters on March 29th, 2018.

articles.title: Nya chocksiffran om antalet döda
articles.summary: Över 700 000 ryska soldater har dödats i kriget, enligt nya bedömningar från ryska exilmedierna Meduza och Mediazona.
articles.body_text: De ryska förlusterna i kriget är betydligt högre än man tidigare trott, enligt nya bedömningar från ryska exilmedierna Meduza och Mediazona . Över 700 000 ryska soldater uppges ha dödats. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Tidigare i månaden läckte uppgifter om att 450 000 ryssar hade mist livet i kriget efter att hackare slagit till mot ryska statistikbyrån Rosstat. Men siffran uppges nu vara betydligt högre än så. Med hjälp av två pro-ukrainska hackergrupper har man försetts med fler källor, inklusive data från Rysslands befolkningsregister och ett statligt datorsystem som skickar information till ryska statistikbyrån Rosstat. Då landar uppskattningen på ”mer än 700 000” döda ryssar i kriget, enligt Meduza. Michael Kofman vid tankesmedjan Carnegie Endowment for International Peace uppgav för New York Times att Ryssland är på god väg att rekrytera runt 409 000 soldater till 2026. Samtidigt förlorar Ryssland fler soldater än man rekryterar. Tankesmedjan Center for Strategic and International Studies i Washington bedömer att 150 000 ukrainska soldater har dött i kriget fram till juni. Expressen erbjuder möjligheten att kommentera artiklar. Vi tar bort inlägg som vi bedömer är olämpliga. Kommentarer granskas inte i förväg. Kommentarerna omfattas inte av utgivaransvaret enligt yttrandefrihetslagen och de är inte heller en del av den grundlagsskyddade databasen expressen.se Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.title: Fembarnsmamman död av optisk illusion
articles.summary: Jody Brown tog fel på en ”optisk illusion”. Det blev den 38-åriga fembarnsmammans död. Nu höjs krav på förändring för att förhindra framtida dödsfall.
articles.body_text: Jody Brown tog fel på en ”optisk illusion”, skriver Daily Mail . Det blev den 38-åriga fembarnsmammans död. Nu höjs krav på förändring för att förhindra framtida dödsfall. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Jody Browns kropp hittades i en kanal i engelska staden Walsall den 3 maj. Hon dödförklarades på platsen. Den 38-åriga fembarnsmamman, som inte kunde simma, hade drunknat. En utredning har nu visat att Brown dog efter att ha misstagit det algtäckta vattnet för en asfalterad stig i vad Daily Mail beskriver som en ”tragisk optisk illusion”. Brown var ”kraftigt berusad” när tragedin inträffade, står det i utredningen. Övervakningskameror filmade henne när hon gick av från en stig och av misstag klev ut i vattendraget. Rättsläkaren Joanne Lees utfärdade en varning till myndigheterna kring bristen på säkerhetsbarriärer och den dåliga belysningen i området. Algerna på vattenytan skapade ”intrycket av en fortsättning på gångstigen och/eller en gräsbevuxen yta” vid tidpunkten för dödsfallet, enligt Lees. Lees berättade att detta hade orsakat flera liknande incidenter tidigare. – Enligt min mening finns det en betydande risk för framtida dödsfall om inte åtgärder vidtas för att ta itu med detta problem, säger Lees. Browns bror Paul Clarke beskrev sin syster som ”utåtriktad och älskad av alla”. – Kanalen är ganska farlig, säger Clarke till BBC.

articles.title: Strandhälls ilska mot V
articles.summary: S-toppen Annika Strandhäll riktar sig till V-veteranen Ulla Andersson efter C-beslutet att återuppta högersamtalen: ”Ni har fullständigt kört sönder detta.”
articles.body_text: S-toppen Annika Strandhäll riktar sig till V-veteranen Ulla Andersson efter Centerpartiets beslut att återuppta högersamtalen. ”Ni har fullständigt kört sönder detta, Ulla. Det är sanningen”, skriver Strandhäll på X. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Centerpartiet återupptar samtalen med M, KD och L. Det meddelade C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist på måndagskvällen. ” Sverige behöver en regering och därför behöver vi öppna fler dörrar, inte stänga några. Vi återupptar därför samtalen med Moderaterna, Kristdemokraterna och Liberalerna ”, skriver Thand Ringqvist i en kommentar till Expressen. Vänsterpartiets vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson beklagar beskedet och anser att de rödgröna borde ha ”synat” Centerpartiets röda linjer före valet. Hon anklagar Centern för att ha ”vänt på en femöring”. ” I skarpt läge var inte en humanare migrationspolitik viktigare än skattesänkningar. De hoppades bara i stället att vi rödgröna skulle överge våra vallöften under press ”, skriver hon. V-veteranen Ulla Andersson är på X kritisk till Centerpartiets sätt att förhandla. ” Det finns de man gärna förhandlar med trots att man kan stå långt ifrån varandra för man kan lita på varandra. Inget fulspel, inget bakom ryggen på en, en ärlig inställning till att försöka lösa det hela. Så finns det de som är tvärtom och jag ser att en sån nu är i farten ”, skriver Andersson, som är tidigare ekonomisk-politisk talesperson för partiet, på X. Det får S-toppen Annika Strandhäll att reagera – och rikta udden mot V. ” Ni har fullständigt kört sönder detta, Ulla. Det är sanningen ”, svarar hon på inlägget.

articles.title: Pekar ut Putins nya skräckvapen
articles.summary: Putins skräckvapen Satan II kan ha tagits i bruk. Det visar en ny analys från tankesmedjan IISS som granskat satellitbilder av ryska militära anläggningar.
articles.body_text: Putins skräckvapen Satan II kan ha tagits i bruk. Det visar en ny analys från tankesmedjan IISS som granskat satellitbilder av ryska militära anläggningar, skriver Newsweek . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Roboten RS-28 Sarmat, även kallad Satan II, har varit under produktion i Ryssland i över ett decennium. Det är en interkontinental ballistisk robot som beskrivs som den mest moderna och största i den ryska kärnvapenarsenalen. Rysslands president Vladimir Putin har hävdat att vapnet kan övervinna även de mest avancerade västerländska försvarssystemen. Analytiker från väst har bedömt att roboten kan ha en maximal räckvidd på cirka 17 000 kilometer vilket skulle placera större delen av Europa och USA inom räckhåll. Ryska statliga medier sade 2016 att vapnet skulle kunna utplåna mål ”stora som Texas eller Frankrike”. Men projektet har ständigt drabbats av bakslag och förseningar. Satan II har haft två lyckade tester, 2022 och maj i år, med flera misslyckade uppskjutningar däremellan. ”Misslyckanden med flygtester har varit mest oroande för Moskva”, skriver tankesmedjan IISS. Men färska satellitbilder, tagna av företaget Vantor och analyserade av IISS, verkar visa aktivitet runt en robotsilo i Ryssland. ”De tyder på att RS-28 Sarmat kan ha börjat tas i bruk”, skriver IISS. Rapporten pekar också på en kran som setts nära silon, ett verktyg som tidigare har använts för att installera stridsspetsar i andra ryska robotar. ”Detta kan tyda på att Sarmat är fullt stridsduglig”, skriver IISS.

articles.title: 24-åringens gåtfulla död på sin semester
articles.summary: 24-åriga Bérengère Deveaux-Cattino dog mystiskt på semestern. ”Jag tänkte: ’Det här är inte normalt, något är fel’”, säger systern Éléonore Deveaux-Cattino.
articles.body_text: 24-åriga Bérengère Deveaux-Cattino dog på semestern. Men dödsorsaken som angivits stämmer inte överens med bevisen, enligt familjen. – Jag tänkte: ”Det här är inte normalt, något är fel”, säger systern Éléonore Deveaux-Cattino till kanadensiska CBC . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Bérengère Deveaux-Cattino reste på semester med sina vänner till Turkiet i juni förra året. 24-åringen skulle fira sin examen från läkarutbildningen. – Hon tyckte att det var ett supervackert och livfullt land, säger hennes syster Éléonore Deveaux-Cattino. Efter att ha checkat in på sitt hotell åt vännerna middag. Men senare vaknade alla upp och mådde väldigt illa. – Plötsligt turades vi om att springa till badrummet för att kräkas tills vi insåg att vad det än var så skulle det inte bara gå över, säger en av Bérengères vänner. I samband med att Bérengère insjuknade kontaktade hon sin syster Éléonore, vilket väckte oro bland hennes familj. Sedan fick systern det fruktansvärda beskedet: – De sade: ”Jag är väldigt ledsen, Éléonore, men din syster är död”. När Bérengère begravdes var hennes dödsorsak fortfarande ett mysterium. Familjen fick så småningom obduktionsrapporten som drog slutsatsen att Bérengère dog av matförgiftning – men det tillbakavisades av rättsläkaren i Quebec. – Rättsläkaren här utförde några tester och hon kunde inte bekräfta att matförgiftning var dödsorsaken eftersom det vanligtvis finns tecken på tarmirritation. Det fanns inga i min systers fall, säger Éléonore.

articles.title: Hegseths tidigare högra hand: ”Du borde avgå”
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth sägs hänga löst. Nu går hans tidigare stabschef Joe Kasper ut och uppmanar honom att avgå. – Jag tror att historien kommer att döma honom betydligt hårdare än vad jag någonsin skulle kunna göra, säger han till Politico.
articles.body_text: Nu går hans tidigare stabschef Joe Kasper ut och uppmanar honom att avgå. – Jag tror att historien kommer att döma honom betydligt hårdare än vad jag någonsin skulle kunna göra, säger han till Politico . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Trumps krigsminister Pete Hegseth har länge varit en nagel i ögat för demokraterna, mycket på grund av hantering av kriget i Iran. Det var därför inte särskilt förvånande att demokraterna bara dagar efter succén i mellanårsvalet började tala om riksrätt för Hegseth. Nu får han även kritik – från egna led. Hans tidigare stabschef Joe Kasper, som avgick i april förra året, uppmanar sin gamla chef att avgå. – Han har gett sitt ego, sin attityd och sin känsla av att ha rätt till särskilda privilegier alldeles för stort utrymme, säger han till Politico . Kasper anlitades av Hegseth i januari 2025, och beskriver sin tid som Hegseths högra hand som ”fullständigt kaos”. Enligt honom är Hegseth ”helt besatt” av sin egen image. – Jag tror att historien kommer att döma honom betydligt hårdare än vad jag någonsin skulle kunna göra, säger han. Hegseth har under sin tid på posten kritiserats hårt av för sin hantering av kriget i Iran – men också för sin relation med kongressen, de som ska ge honom mer pengar. – Han har inte bara bränt broarna till kongressen. Han har bombat dem med napalm. Han kommer att kvävas, och det kommer inte att ske långsamt. Han kommer att kvävas snabbt, säger han. Hegseth har hela tiden fått stöd av Trump. Så sent som i november röstade representanthuset ner ett förslag om att ställa Hegseth inför riksrätt. Det fallet kommer troligen tas upp igen nästa år när demokraterna har full kontroll i kongressen.

articles.title: C återupptar samtal med M, KD och L
articles.summary: C återupptar samtalen med högerpartierna. ”Sverige behöver en regering och därför behöver vi öppna fler dörrar, inte stänga några”, skriver partiledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist i en kommentar till Expressen.
articles.body_text: C återupptar samtalen med högerpartierna. ”Sverige behöver en regering och därför behöver vi öppna fler dörrar, inte stänga några”, skriver partiledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist i en kommentar till Expressen. V-toppen Ida Gabrielsson ”beklagar C:s sidbyte”. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Enligt Thand Ringqvist har C inte fått några tydliga besked från V som gör det möjligt att gå vidare med en regering ledd av Magdalena Andersson. ” Centerpartiet har gått långt för att hitta en lösning och ytterligare omfattande eftergifter för att få Vänsterpartiet till förhandlingsbordet är inte aktuella ”, skriver hon. Samtidigt betonar partiledaren att man ”inte tänker låta regeringsbildningen fastna”. ” Sverige behöver en regering och därför behöver vi öppna fler dörrar, inte stänga några. Vi återupptar därför samtalen med Moderaterna, Kristdemokraterna och Liberalerna. Centerpartiet är fortsatt berett att ta ansvar, söka lösningar och samtala med båda sidor för att Sverige ska få en ny regering ”, fortsätter hon. Enligt Expressens uppgifter har C:s partistyrelse och riksdagsgrupp haft ett möte under måndagskvällen , där man bland annat diskuterat ett regeringssamarbete med de borgerliga partierna. V:s vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson ”beklagar” vad hon beskriver som ”C:s sidbyte”. ” Men ännu mer att vi inte hjälptes åt att syna hur förankrade C egentligen var innan valet ”, skriver Gabrielsson på X . Hon anklagar partiet för att ha hoppats på att de rödgröna partierna under press skulle överge sina vallöften.

articles.title: Elevernas skräckvälde: ”Tortyrliknande” våld
articles.summary: Prefekten stod högst i rang. Men det var, enligt åtalet, strafförmannen och viceprefekten som utförde de grövsta, ”tortyrliknande” brotten mot yngre elever på Sigtunaskolan.
articles.body_text: Men det var, enligt åtalet, strafförmannen och viceprefekten som utförde de grövsta, ”tortyrliknande” brotten mot yngre elever. Slag med golfklubba och metallskohorn, sexuella kränkningar och dödshot misstänks ha varit några av inslagen i skräckväldet på Sigtunaskolan. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den 7 oktober i år berättade en elev på Sigtunaskolan för kuratorn att han och flera andra pojkar hade utsatts för våld, kränkningar och övergrepp av två äldre elever på skolan några dagar tidigare. Händelsen polisanmäldes. De utpekade gärningsmännen var en 17-åring som enligt utredningen hade titeln ”strafförman” och en 18-åring som kallades ”viceprefekt” på ett av den anrika internatskolans elevhem. Fyra yngre pojkar ska ha tvingats in på viceprefektens rum och utsatts för våld och kränkningar: De tvingades leka en lek där en pojke satt med sin nakna rumpa mot en annan pojkes ansikte, varpå vatten hälldes mellan den ene pojkens skinkor och in i munnen på den andre. Delvis avklädda tvingades de posera i olika ställningar medan viceprefekten och strafförmannen slog dem med bland annat en golfklubba, en flippflopp-toffla och ett metallskohorn. De tvingades också slå varandra, göra sugmärken och utföra sexuella handlingar på varandra. Viceprefekten och strafförmannen ska ha stoppat blöta papperstussar i pojkarnas munnar och påstått att tussarna varit i toaletten och hade avföring på sig. Strafförmannen ska ha sagt att pojkarna skulle dö om de berättade för någon vad de varit med om. Åklagaren Lisa dos Santos skriver i stämningsansökan: ”Gärningen är att bedöma som grov eftersom de tilltalade visat särskild hänsynslöshet med förnedrande och tortyrliknande inslag, använt flera tillhyggen och anspelat på både ett våldskapital och en maktposition i förhållande till målsägandena.”
